title: NOT_REPORTED
abstract_summary: Compares SLAM front-ends for a ground robot by evaluating trajectory accuracy against a VICON motion-capture reference. The stated comparison reports an average translation error of 0.071 m for Hector SLAM against 0.059 m for Cartographer SLAM, so the two explainable front-ends are separated by roughly one centimetre on this trajectory.
problem_setting: Evaluates positioning accuracy without relying on GNSS, using onboard sensing and an external motion-capture reference in a controlled environment. The denial scenario is treated as a general GNSS-absent setting rather than a named jammed or indoor application.
historical_context: Positioned in the SLAM comparison literature: the paper benchmarks Hector SLAM and Cartographer SLAM, two long-standing 2D LiDAR SLAM systems, and reports their accuracy against a VICON reference rather than proposing a new estimator.
core_idea: Run two established SLAM systems on the same GNSS-denied trajectory and quantify their positioning accuracy against motion-capture ground truth. The contribution is the measured comparison rather than a new algorithm.
algorithmic_components: scan matching; occupancy grid map; loop closure; motion-capture ground-truth evaluation
claimed_novelty: [paraphrase] The paper presents a measured accuracy comparison of established SLAM front-ends against motion-capture ground truth, rather than a new estimator.
extraction_source: PDF body text, sentence reporting the average translation error (ATE) of Hector SLAM and Cartographer SLAM against a VICON motion-capture reference; sentence also appears in the master CSV notes field
notes: PARTIAL RECORD - the identity block (authors, title, year, venue, doi, url) was not yet read off the first page and is written as NOT_REPORTED rather than guessed. best_ate_rmse carries the better of the two reported systems (Cartographer, 0.059 m) with the competing value preserved in other_metric_value, so nothing is lost. environment_category is Mixed because the paper does not name a scenario. qa_* and citation_tier are copied verbatim from extracted_master_v2.csv at commit time, not authored here.
